premise.headline: A grudge gets uncorked at Thanksgiving.

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Notes of Murder
jokes.joke: I went to a murder mystery at a winery, and I solved it before dessert. Everyone else was asking who had access to the cellar. I said, “The winemaker did it.” They said, “Why?” I said, “Because he described the victim as having notes of oak and a surprisingly long finish.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Grape Expectations
jokes.joke: My ex became a winemaker. I went to his tasting room, swirled the glass like I knew what I was doing, and said, 'It's good. Earthy. A little bitter.' He goes, 'That's actually quite sweet.' And I thought — yeah, that tracks. I've been telling people he's bitter for three years. Turns out I'm the one who can't let it go. I'm the wine.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Aged to Perfection
jokes.joke: People say I need to learn to let things go, but I just can't do it. I treat my grudges the way a master vintner treats a fine wine. I lock them in a cold, dark cellar in my brain. I rotate them occasionally. I wait ten to fifteen years until they are perfectly, exquisitely bitter. And then, right when nobody expects it, I uncork that bad boy at Thanksgiving dinner and force my entire family to taste it.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Grudge Match
jokes.joke: Folks, I'm awful at forgiving people. My buddy totaled my car last year and I still bring it up every time we grab a beer. He finally snaps, 'Dude, move on already!' and I get all defensive: 'Move on? You're the one who turned my Honda into modern art, Picasso!' At this point, holding grudges isn't a flaw—it's my cardio.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: The Case of the Missing Chill
jokes.joke: I get way too defensive. The other day my friend asked who finished the last slice of pizza, and I panicked like it was a full-on whodunit. I’m standing there sweating, giving alibis, checking for fingerprints… and then I remember I live alone. I basically interrogated myself over my own snack crimes.

scores.comment: Clear setup and a nice self-inverting turn, though the final line is more clever than laugh-heavy.
Strongest stage rhythm in the batch, with clean escalation and a concrete Thanksgiving payoff; the wine/grudge metaphor is familiar but well executed.
Readable and in form, but the Picasso line and cardio tag feel generic and the turn does not sharpen much beyond the setup.
Competent mild joke with a clear defensive whodunit angle, but the live-alone turn is familiar and slightly muddied by the friend setup.

Clean concept and the wine-tasting language as murder evidence is a nice inversion, but the punchline lands softly; 'long finish' is the only real turn and it feels like the joke ends where it should accelerate.
Strong escalation and the Thanksgiving uncorking is a genuinely satisfying payoff. The grudge-as-aging-wine conceit is familiar in broad strokes, but the execution gives it real stage energy.
The Picasso line is a solid mid-joke beat, but 'holding grudges is my cardio' is a well-worn closer that deflates the finish.
'I live alone' is a genuinely clean reversal and 'interrogated myself over my own snack crimes' is a fun closing image. Concise and well-timed.
Solidly constructed but relies on a familiar trope; gets a mild smile but lacks a strong, unexpected turn.
Starts with a relatable premise but devolves into a weak, introspective metaphor that does not land as a joke.
Heavy reliance on dated phrasings limits the humor; reads more like a sitcom caricature than fresh stand-up.
Demonstrates competent pacing and escalation, but the twist is heavily overused in modern stand-up.
Solid wine pun but predictable trope.
Cute self-own twist, mildly relatable.
Strong extended metaphor with sharp family dinner payoff.
Relatable visual bit with clean self-aware snap.
Clean structure and a clear turn, but the punchline is predictable and mild.
Strong first-person framing and a neat self-reveal; lands as a mild but real joke.
Well-built metaphor with a clear escalation; funny image, though slightly long.
Solid premise and rhythm, but the turn is familiar and the punchline is light.
